subject: Procurement & budget owner mapping - ACME Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acme.com>, Procurement Ops <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps - procurement / budget owner mapping

Hi Alice / Tom -

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary from our discovery
- Primary use case: embedding search + summarization for internal knowledge base (product + legal docs).
- Expected start-of-PoC: mid-April, 2-3 teams, ~50k tokens/day peak.
- Success metrics: latency < 250ms p50, cost per 1k tokens target ~ $X (we'll provide numbers in quote).

Procurement / commercial questions we flagged:
1) Procurement path: Do you prefer PO via Ariba/Procurement system or will charge card be used for initial pilot?
2) Economic buyer / finance sponsor: who signs off on contracts and budget? Who is the finance approver that will own the P&L?
3) Signatory: who is the legal signatory (name/title)?
4) Marketplace interest: are you interested in purchasing via AWS Marketplace / GCP Marketplace?

Attachments: Redwood-Procurement-Checklist.xlsx (procurement asks checklist), SOW-draft.pdf (scope draft), ACME-quote-Redwood.pdf (placeholder quote)

Proposed next steps
- ACME to confirm procurement path (PO vs card) and provide contact for economic buyer / finance sponsor by EOD Friday (3/27).
- Redwood to send formal quote and marketplace options by 3/26.
- If PO: provide procurement intake form and SOC2 + security pack.

Please reply with the names/emails for the budget owner and signatory so we can populate the intake form and align internal approvals. Happy to jump on a short follow-up with procurement if helpful.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood-Procurement-Checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
Attachment: SOW-draft.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acme.com>, Procurement Ops <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - procurement / budget owner mapping

Hi Marissa -

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from procurement side: 
- Procurement path: ACME prefers a PO through our Ariba instance for anything > $10k/month; for pilots under that threshold we can use P-card. For enterprise contracts we'll need a standard PO + supplier onboarding.
- Finance sponsor / economic buyer: Tom Rivera (cc'd) is the finance sponsor who'll sign off on budget.
- Signatory: Final signature will be by our CFO, Elena Morris (elena.morris@acme.com). Procurement Ops handles intake.
- Marketplace: We typically evaluate Marketplace options (AWS Marketplace) but it's not a blocker - we just need to understand pricing differences and marketplace fees.

Timeline: procurement intake + review usually takes 2-4 weeks once we have completed paperwork and pricing details. If you can share the procurement intake form and SOC2 + security artifacts, Procurement Ops will triage internally. Attaching our intake form.

Attaching: ACME-procurement-intake-form.pdf

Tom, can you confirm if we need any additional legal terms or if standard T&Cs are OK for the pilot?

Best,
Alice
Head of Platform Partnerships
ACME Corp
Attachment: ACME-procurement-intake-form.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acme.com>, Procurement Ops <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - procurement / budget owner mapping

Thanks Alice - that's helpful. We'll proceed with two parallel tracks: 

1) Pilot (short-term): provide card option to get started quickly. We can invoice monthly and accept P-card for the pilot.
2) Long-term (procurement/PO): prepare procurement intake & SOC2/security pack and finalize PO workflow for production.

Action items (Redwood):
- I'll send a formal quote (itemized by model/throughput) and a concise one-pager on marketplace vs direct billing by EOD 3/26.
- Vivek will prepare the SOC2 + security artifact bundle and a short implementation SLA for the pilot.
- We'll pre-fill your intake form with the budget owner fields once Tom confirms the approver details.

Tom - could you confirm the budget owner (owner of the budget line) versus the signatory (CFO)? If different, can you share the name and email of the budget owner so we can map approvals?

Link to SOC2 & docs: https://redwood.app/security/soc2-report

Attachment: ACME-quote-Redwood.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: prep for ACME procurement intake & budget mapping

Marissa / Aditya -

Following Alice's notes, I'll assemble the security pack (SOC2, encryption/KMS notes, data retention policy) and a short one-pager that explains PO vs Marketplace differences and key timing expectations.

Requests from my side:
- Marissa: please confirm estimated TCV for the pilot (monthly run-rate / expected commit if this converts) so I can tailor the pricing fallback and recommended PO terms.
- Aditya: can you prepare a prioritized list of features/scope in the SOW-draft.pdf that match the pilot success metrics (latency, uptime, token volumes)? I want us to be prepared for procurement questions on RTO/RPO and support SLAs.

I'll also paste the HubSpot deal link and flag for AE/CS to own the procurement thread: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-2026-001

Thanks,
Vivek
